# BlazePhoenix-Staking

> A single-asset staking and lending protocol for the EVM where the collateral,
> the borrowed asset, and the reward token are **the same token (BZPX)** — so no
> price oracle exists anywhere in the system, and an entire class of attacks is
> structurally absent. Solvency is not audited after the fact: every value-moving
> transaction proves it, or reverts. Written in Solidity.

This file follows the llmstxt.org convention: it is addressed to AI agents,
crawlers, and language models reading this repository. Human-facing docs are in
`README.md`.

  protocol is designed to receive a share of that router's fees as real yield.

## The one equation the whole protocol obeys

    balanceOf(contract) + totalBadDebt
      ==  (totalStaked − totalDebt)                      // net principal held
        +  rewardReserve                                 // unspent emission
        +  protocolReserve                               // protocol revenue
        +  (totalRewardDistributed − totalRewardsPaid)   // accrued, unpaid

The right-hand side is `_owed()`. **Solvency ⇔ balance ≥ owed.** Every
value-moving entry point is wrapped in a `conserves` modifier that snapshots both
sides before the body and requires the *change* in real balance to equal the
*change* in what the ledger claims. A transaction that would let the books claim
more than the contract holds **reverts atomically**. An insolvent state is
unreachable, not merely observable.

## What makes it different

- **No oracle, by construction.** Collateral and debt are the same asset, so
  there is no price to feed and nothing to manipulate. Oracle manipulation,
  unfair price liquidation, liquidation MEV, and read-only reentrancy against a
  price read are all absent surfaces — not mitigated risks.
- **Anyone can verify solvency on-chain, for free.** `isSolvent()`, `backing()`,
  `owed()`, `collateralRatio()`, and `solvency()` (every term of the identity in
  one struct) require no indexer, no trust, and no off-chain watcher.
- **100% autonomous maintenance.** No keeper bot and no admin button. Every
  ordinary user transaction drives a gas-bounded, self-sizing sweep over two
  rotating registries — borrowers and lockers — that liquidates what is
  underwater, normalises expired locks, and pays the seizure surplus to whoever
  carried the gas.
- **Zero backdoor.** No admin sweep of principal. Reserve withdrawals are bounded
  by protocol revenue and can only ever reach an immutable treasury address. The
  emergency hatch is pull-only.
- **Two halt paths, one of them objective.** A guardian may halt at discretion;
  separately, *anyone* may trip the breaker, but only when the chain itself
  proves insolvency (`balance + dust < owed`) — an un-spoofable condition,
  reversible once it clears.

## Emission — 180M BZPX on a biennial-halving curve (v4)

Period `p` (0-indexed, two years each) emits `90M >> p`: 90M in years 1–2, 45M in
years 3–4, 22.5M in years 5–6, and so on. The total is exact by construction, not
by calibration: Σ 90M/2^p = 180M.

Cumulative emission is a **closed form** — one division, two shifts, one
multiplication; no loop, no oracle, no exp/log:

    emitted(t) = (TOTAL − (TOTAL >> p)) + (R0 >> p)·(t − start − p·PERIOD),
    p = ⌊(t − start) / PERIOD⌋

- The accumulator distributes the **delta of that curve**, never `rate × elapsed`.
  With a time-varying rate the rectangle approximation would let a window
  straddling a halving boundary be paid at whichever period's rate a passing
  transaction happened to land in. The delta of a monotone cumulative curve is
  the exact integral, independent of who touches the contract and when.
- The same expression backs the pending-rewards view, so **a quote read in a
  block equals what a claim in that block pays**.
- The programme closes after 8 periods (16 years) with 255/256 of the budget
  emitted; the exact `180M >> 8 = 703,125 BZPX` tail, plus anything stranded by
  empty windows, is recoverable to the treasury and to nobody else.
- `emittedAt(timestamp)` exposes the entire curve on-chain, so the schedule is
  independently verifiable rather than merely documented.

## Security properties (invariants)

- **Master Conservation Identity** — enforced per transaction, not audited after.
- **Deterministic emission, no backlog capture** — when nothing is staked the
  clock advances but the accumulator does not, so a latecomer can never harvest
  a window they were absent for. That emission strands in reserve, recoverable.
- **Boost is the price of illiquidity, and it expires on time** — an expired lock
  is re-priced to 1.00x on both axes: no code path can derive a weight from an
  elapsed commitment, and the locker sweep sheds that weight from the global
  denominators without the idle position ever being touched.
- **Single-writer boost accounting** — one function writes both global
  denominators; no path, including the emergency hatch, can desync them.
- **Interest is stamped at the rate that prevailed** — the index is advanced
  before any write that could move the rate, so no caller can choose the rate at
  which somebody else's accrued interest is charged.
- **Mandatory locked staking** — 90 to 2555 days, extend-only, and withdrawal
  requires the position to be fully repaid. No early exit, therefore no penalty.
- **Bounded gas, unconditionally** — the maintenance sweep's worst case per
  transaction is a fixed iteration ceiling regardless of registry size.

The engineering report `docs/INVARIANTS_AND_TIME.md` documents the seven
historical defects, why six of them left the books perfectly balanced, and the
rules that fall out of that — the central one being that a conservation
invariant answers *how much*, never *who* or *when*.

## Verification

- **Foundry suites** — unit, fuzz, and structural invariants (including
  `invariant_everyLiveCommitmentIsTracked`).
- **Nine real-EVM suites** (`@ethereumjs/vm`, fully offline) — integrity,
  adversarial vectors, canonical DeFi attack vectors, boost/lock-expiry
  regression, state dimensions, metamorphic relations with scaling studies,
  boundary reporting, and a self-audit that treats each past remediation as a
  suspect.
- **CI** runs all of it on every push, plus an EIP-170 deploy-size gate.
- **Responsible disclosure is credited** — see the Hall of Fame in `README.md`.
